newsitem.title: USA: WALL ST WEEK AHEAD/Stocks brace for earnings test.
newsitem.headline: WALL ST WEEK AHEAD/Stocks brace for earnings test.

text.p: A slew of corporate earnings will test Wall Street's mettle this week, but buyers are not expected to vanish any time soon.
With many stocks topping record highs, the market will scrutinise earnings reports, dissecting them for clues about the third quarter and the rest of the year.
But, provided companies keep posting solid earnings, stock prices should march higher.

"The basic trend is that people want to buy stocks," said Roy Blumberg, chief investment strategist at Josephthal Lyon & Ross. "Most investors in the market have never seen a bear market and won't believe it until they see a correction which lasts more than a week and is over 10 percent.
Falling bond yields, reflecting hopes for lower interest rates, would also give stocks help, analysts said.
Because stock prices are so high, they need the added boost from lower bond yields in order to tack on gains, analysts say.

Recently, yields have dropped on the thinking that inflation is tame, growth is steady and interest rates are not going up any time soon. The 30-year Treasury bond finished the week with a yield of 6.53 percent.
"It wouldn't surprise me to see the Dow go over 8,000 this week," said Harry Laubscher, a market analyst at Tucker Anthony. "Earnings and (the) bond market will dominate."
The Dow Jones Industrial Average finished up 35.06 points at 7,921.82 Friday, after a week which saw several of its component stocks report better-than-expected results.
For the week, the Dow rose 26.01 points.
"The only thing that seems to drag this market down is profit-taking," said Thom Brown, managing director of Rutherford Brown and Catherwood.
But with stocks trading at such lofty levels, companies reporting disappointing earnings will be punished, they said.
"Wall Street is completely unforgiving when it comes to poor earnings reports," Blumberg said.
Among the multitude of companies reporting this week, Intel Corp. will be a highlight Tuesday.
The chip maker was expected to report $1.80 per share for its second quarter, compared with $1.17 per share in the year-ago quarter, according to a First Call service survey of analysts.

Merck & Co. Inc. will also report this week. The drug manufacturer, which is one of the 30 stocks comprising the Dow Jones Industrial index, was expected to earn 95 cents per share, compared with 80 cents per share in last year's second quarter.
Economic data will also give direction to markets, analysts said.
The Consumer Price Index for June, an indication of inflation, is due Wednesday. It was expected to rise 0.2 percent, compared with a 0.1 percent rise in May.
Industrial production for June was also slated to come out Wednesday. It was expected to rise 0.2 percent vs. a 0.4 percent gain in May.
